source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Water management under the System of Rice Intensification (SRI): drain the field well, but do not keep a large depth of standing water during the crop's active growth stage, especially during tillering. After transplanting, water depth in the field should generally not exceed about 2-3 cm; alternating wet and dry conditions (letting the field dry down and then re-wetting, rather than continuous flooding) is preferred - keeping the soil just moist is considered sufficient. This water regime helps suppress weed growth, helps the rice plant take up soil nutrients more efficiently, supports decomposition of organic matter in the soil, and encourages the rice plant to produce more tillers. Fields should also be kept free of weeds, since weeds compete directly with the rice crop. Where feasible, farmers are encouraged to dig a small water-storage basin within the field, roughly 20 m by 10 m, which can hold water reserves and also be used to raise fish.

Fertilizer/soil-nutrition management: farmers are encouraged to prioritize natural (organic) fertilizer strongly, because it makes soil more friable/fertile, helps the soil retain moisture longer, increases overall soil fertility, reduces the amount that needs to be spent on chemical fertilizer, and helps protect the environment. Recommended organic fertilizer sources include animal manure, compost, and green manures (legume-family plants, mimosa/sensitive-plant species, and azolla water fern). Rice straw and rice stubble left after harvest also return significant nutrients to paddy soil and should be well incorporated/composted into the field rather than burned. A general application rate given is 10-20 tonnes per hectare of manure or compost, incorporated during the final plowing pass. Fresh green manure or fresh plant residue should be incorporated into the soil 10-15 days before transplanting, to allow it enough time to decompose well before the rice is planted.
